correctness.rationale: The source polytope has exactly all signed edge facets because the graph is bipartite and every vertex belongs to an edge. Coordinate sign symmetry and unique John ellipsoid force zero-centered diagonal shape, and support in a signed edge normal equals sqrt(u_a+u_b). The proposed positive rational axes satisfy all edge constraints. Pendant multipliers (p_i+1)/p_i reproduce every gradient 1/u_v exactly, yielding the global concavity inequality (9) and strict uniqueness. Product determinants yield volume; elementary support distances yield contact screening, the bound 5/6, and exact count. The actual standalone checker replayed successfully with 16,977 exact bipartite graphs and 34 independent numerical optimizations. No infinite assertion relies on finite tests.

value.rationale: The result is a natural infinite family and graph surgery invariance of a canonical Euclidean extremal invariant. It states that arbitrarily many new genuine core-edge facets cannot alter the unique maximal inscribed ellipsoid, with a sharp one-versus-two-leaf tangency transition, explicit uniform clearance, and heterogeneous leaf-dependent axes. This explains a nonobvious structure across all bipartite core topologies rather than recomputing a narrow finite table. The private-leaf threshold is sharp for unconditional edge-insensitivity.
